title: Orchestrator leadership flap during staged model rollout causing capacity evictions and rollback starvation
creator: Maya Thompson
description: During a staged rollout of model v7.3 -> v8.0 we observed a cascade where transient orchestrator leader elections and staggered pod drain sequences caused capacity to temporarily drop below the rollback quota, leading to evictions, degraded latency, and failed automatic rollback. This ticket documents the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied in-the-moment, and proposed action items to prevent recurrence.
impact: ~12m of degraded tail latency (p95 increased from 120ms to 420ms) for several customers on dedicated pools, 3 customer-facing requests returned 503s, and an automated rollback attempt stalled and did not converge within SLOs. Estimated token loss equivalent cost: medium-high. No data corruption.
detection: On-call pager triggered by latency alert from runtime-2.4 per-route SLOs (p95 exceed) at 2026-03-01T14:22:03Z. Auto-scaling alerts and eviction metrics spiked shortly after. Customer support ticket triage flagged 3 customers reporting 503s.
timeline:
- 2026-03-01T14:15Z: Canary rollout started (v7.3 -> v8.0) with staged traffic window and drain hooks enabled.
- 2026-03-01T14:20Z: First leader election observed in orchestrator zone A after transient API heartbeat lag.
- 2026-03-01T14:21Z: A subset of worker pods entered preStop drain but leader handoff completed slowly; drain coordinator retried drains.
- 2026-03-01T14:22Z: Autoscaler reacted to perceived capacity drop, initiated scale-up but new capacity delayed by node provisioning.
- 2026-03-01T14:23–14:27Z: Eviction events increased as eviction controller reclaimed resources; some pinned route assignments could not be rebalanced because rollout controller awaited leader lock.
- 2026-03-01T14:28Z: Automated rollback triggered but rollback goroutine blocked waiting for rollout index sync and leader confirmation.
- 2026-03-01T14:29Z: Operators applied emergency partial-rollback and increased healthcheck grace windows; leader stabilized.
- 2026-03-01T14:34Z: Traffic returned to normal, autoscaler backfilled capacity; incident resolved.
root_cause: A combination of three independent but interacting faults: 1) Orchestrator leader election sensitivity to short heartbeat jitter (5–8s) caused leadership flap during a critical staged drain window. 2) Pod drain ordering and preStop hooks were not coordinated across the rollout controller, allowing too many capacity-bearing replicas to be removed concurrently. 3) Rollback path requires fresh rollout index confirmation from the leader; when leader was unstable the rollback goroutine stalled (blocked on leader-ack), preventing fallback before autoscaler replenished capacity.
mitigations_applied:
- Increased healthcheck grace_period on the impacted pools for 30 minutes.
- Temporarily paused the ongoing staged rollout and reverted to previous stable pinned version for high-impact customer routes.
- Kicked manual leader reconciliation and restarted a subset of orchestrator replicas to break the election loop.
- Adjusted autoscaler thresholds to avoid aggressive eviction during recovery window.
long_term_action_items: Introduce a leader-stable window feature: require a configurable quorum-stability period (default 30s) before rollout-critical operations (drain, index commit, rollback) proceed.

Implement coordinated drain sequencing: rollout controller should compute drain budget based on real-time available capacity and orchestrator leader state; prevent concurrent drains that exceed budget.

Add a non-blocking rollback path: allow rollback goroutines to proceed with a degraded confirmation mode (with audit trail) if leader confirmation cannot be obtained within Xs, plus automatic verification after leader returns.
Add synthetic canary traffic generator during staged rollouts to exercise autoscaler and detect capacity fragility before broad promotion.
Improve observability: new dashboard panels for 'leader-election-rate', 'drain-budget', and 'rollback-block-duration' and alerts when rollback-block-duration > 5s.
Create a post-incident runbook entry: step-by-step for leader-flap during rollout including safe pause criteria and rollback bypass steps.
Stress-test node provisioning and autoscaler timing in staging with injected leader-election noise to validate new safety guards.
Document migration plan to rollout controller v2 that uses lease-based leader locks with pessimistic timeouts and persistent rollout index checkpoints.
Add an integration test to CI that simulates concurrent drain + leader-election and asserts no more than N replicas are removed.
Share incident summary with SRE, Platform, and Console teams and schedule a cross-team retro to align rollout-related SLAs and knobs.
owner_notes: Primary owner: Luis Gomez (assignee). Will coordinate with SRE (Aisha Khan) on leader election tuning and with Product for rollback UX changes. Temp mitigation (healthcheck grace and manual revert) is in place; do not re-enable staged rollout for v8.0 until action items 1–3 are implemented.

notes: This incident highlights a systemic ordering dependency between control-plane leader stability and data-plane rollout safety. The immediate fixes are low risk; the long-term remediation requires cross-team design work. Recommend elevating rollout safety as a Q2 priority for SRE/Platform/Runtime.
